newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine police kill three in "ice" sting.
newsitem.headline: Philippine police kill three in "ice" sting.

text.p: Philippine police shot dead three suspected members of an international drug-trafficking ring in a gunbattle in Manila early on Tuesday, police said.

The trio -- a Hong Kong Chinese citizen, a Taiwanese and an unidentified man -- were in a car travelling to meet a policeman posing as a buyer in a sting operation when anti-narcotics officers confronted them in the Makati business district, a police report said.
The suspects opened fire and police shot back, killing all three in an exchange near a cemetery, it said.
Police said they found 25 plastic bags of methamphetamine hydrochloride, or "ice", worth $385,000 and three pistols in the suspects' car.
Anti-narcotics command chief General Rex Piad said the three men were believed to be members of a Hong Kong "triad" supplying "ice" to Filipino buyers.
Police two months ago arrested a Hong Kong Chinese man and confiscated $25 million worth of "ice" and morphine in one of the biggest seizures of illegal drugs ever in the Philippines.

Since the Philippines restored the death penalty in 1993 for drug trafficking and other so-called "heinous crimes", local courts have sentenced 17 drug dealers to death, including a Japanese and two Taiwanese.
None of the sentences have yet been confirmed by the Supreme Court.
